subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of locus of P, if the ratio of the distance from P to (5, −4) and (7, 6) is 2 : 3.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 1 LOCUS, Short Answer question 3, book p.134. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split 1+1+2 rewards the two method moves separately — turning the ratio into 9PA² = 4PB², then putting the distance formula in — and gives the remaining two marks to the expansion that produces the circle, which is where the arithmetic is lost. The unmarked opening step names the moving point and carries no mark of its own. Answer cross-checked by substituting the point (29/5, 0), which divides the join of the two given points in the ratio 2 : 3 and satisfies the final equation. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11 to Q18 at 4 marks each, answer any 6 of 8, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you would do with the ratio first, and name the shape the locus turns out to be.

steps.label: Take the locus point
steps.margin_note: No mark of its own. A ratio question, not a sum — one squaring clears both roots, so no square root ever has to be isolated.
steps.memory_tip: A ratio, not a sum — one squaring clears both roots, so no root is ever isolated.
lines: Let P = (x, y) be a point on the locus.

recall.must_convey: That the moving point is named P = (x, y) and the two fixed points are written down.
accept: let P be x comma y
take the locus point as P x y
P equals x comma y is on the locus
locus point ni P x y ga teesukovali
name the moving point P with coordinates x and y

steps.why: Every locus question starts the same way: the moving point gets coordinates, and the condition is then written in terms of those coordinates.
common_mistakes: Giving the moving point fixed numbers instead of (x, y).
Mixing up which points are fixed and which one moves.

steps.label: Write the given condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Cross-multiply the ratio first, then square both sides together. Squaring 3PA = 2PB gives 9PA² = 4PB² — the numbers get squared too.
steps.memory_tip: Cross-multiply first, then square. The numbers get squared as well: 3 and 2 become 9 and 4.

recall.must_convey: That the ratio is cross-multiplied to 3PA = 2PB and then squared to 9PA² = 4PB².
accept: cross multiply to get three P A equals two P B then square it
P A by P B is two by three so three P A is two P B
square both sides to get nine P A squared equals four P B squared
ratio ni cross multiply chesi square cheyyali
nine times P A squared equals four times P B squared

steps.why: A ratio of two distances squares cleanly in one step, so both square roots disappear together and no term is left outside.
common_mistakes: Writing 2PA = 3PB, which turns the ratio upside down.
Squaring to 3PA² = 2PB² and leaving the numbers unsquared.

steps.label: Substitute the distances
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put the squared distance formula into both brackets. The two fixed points share no coordinate here, so all four numbers change between the brackets.
steps.memory_tip: Expand each bracket on its own line first — four numbers change between the two brackets, not one.

recall.must_convey: That both squared distances are written in coordinates, with 9 multiplying the A bracket and 4 the B bracket.
accept: substitute the distance formula into both sides keeping the nine and the four outside
put x minus five whole squared plus y plus four whole squared on the left
expand both brackets in coordinates
distance formula substitute chesi rendu brackets expand cheyyali
nine into the A bracket and four into the B bracket

steps.why: Expanding each bracket on its own line keeps the six terms visible before the 9 and the 4 are multiplied in, which is where most sign slips happen.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the first term of a bracket by 9 or by 4.

steps.label: Simplify to the locus
steps.margin_note: The last two marks. The x² and y² coefficients survive equal (both 5), so this locus is a circle. Check: the point (29/5, 0) divides the join of A and B in the ratio 2 : 3 and satisfies the final equation.
steps.memory_tip: The x² and y² coefficients survive equal, so the locus is a circle — never a straight line.

recall.must_convey: That collecting terms gives the circle 5x² + 5y² − 34x + 120y + 29 = 0.
accept: collect all the terms to get five x squared plus five y squared minus thirty four x plus one twenty y plus twenty nine equals zero
the x squared and y squared coefficients are both five so it is a circle
bring everything to one side and simplify
anni terms okavaipuku teesukoni simplify chesthe circle vasthundi
the locus is a circle

steps.why: When two distances are in a fixed ratio that is not 1 : 1, the locus is always a circle. Equal x² and y² coefficients are the sign that the algebra landed right.
